description: The opening chapter of al-Ājurrūmiyyah: what speech (kalām) is, and its three constituent parts - the noun, the verb, and the particle.

lessons.titleEnglish: The Definition of Kalām and Its Three Types
lessons.matnArabic: الْكَلاَمُ: هُوَ اللَّفْظُ الْمُرَكَّبُ الْمُفِيدُ بِالْوَضْعِ. وَأَقْسَامُهُ ثَلاَثَةٌ: اسْمٌ، وَفِعْلٌ، وَحَرْفٌ جَاءَ لِمَعْنًى.
lessons.translation: Kalām (speech) is a composed utterance that conveys a complete meaning, established by [linguistic] convention. Its types are three: a noun (ism), a verb (fiʿl), and a particle (ḥarf) that comes for a [grammatical] meaning.
lessons.explanation: Ibn Ājurrūm opens the matn by defining the very subject of the book: kalām, i.e. meaningful Arabic speech. Four conditions are packed into the definition. It must be an 'utterance' (لفظ) - actual sound, not merely an idea. It must be 'composed' (مركّب) - made of at least two words. It must be 'meaningful' (مفيد) - the listener can stop at it and it makes complete sense on its own, unlike 'in the house' alone. And it must be 'by convention' (بالوضع) - Arabic words, not random noises or a foreign language a listener does not know. Every word in Arabic falls into exactly one of three categories: اسم (a word denoting a person, place, thing or idea, with no notion of time), فعل (a word denoting an action tied to a time), and حرف (a particle that only has meaning when linked to a noun or verb, such as 'in', 'from', or 'and').

keyTerms.definition: A composed, meaningful utterance in Arabic, established by linguistic convention.
A word indicating a person, place, or thing, without reference to a particular time.
A word indicating an action or event tied to a particular tense (past, present, or command).
A word that only carries meaning in combination with a noun or verb, e.g. prepositions and conjunctions.

examples.translation: From (a particle of meaning only when attached to a noun).

recallQuestions.questionEnglish: What are the three types of kalām (word categories) in Arabic?
recallQuestions.correctAnswer: اسم، وفعل، وحرف جاء لمعنى (noun, verb, and particle that carries a meaning)

recallQuestions.questionEnglish: Which of the following is NOT a condition packed into the definition of kalām?

recallQuestions.correctAnswer: Because a single isolated word, on its own, is not called kalām in the technical sense - it must be composed of at least two words.

memorisationSections.arabicText: الْكَلاَمُ: هُوَ اللَّفْظُ الْمُرَكَّبُ الْمُفِيدُ بِالْوَضْعِ. وَأَقْسَامُهُ ثَلاَثَةٌ: اسْمٌ، وَفِعْلٌ، وَحَرْفٌ جَاءَ لِمَعْنًى.
memorisationSections.translation: Kalām is a composed, meaningful utterance, established by convention. Its types are three: a noun, a verb, and a particle that comes for a meaning.
memorisationSections.transliteration: al-kalāmu huwa al-lafẓu al-murakkabu al-mufīdu bi-l-waḍʿ. wa-aqsāmuhu thalāthah: ismun, wa fiʿlun, wa ḥarfun jāʾa li-maʿnā.

lessons.matnArabic: فَالاِسْمُ يُعْرَفُ بِالْخَفْضِ، وَالتَّنْوِينِ، وَدُخُولِ الأَلِفِ وَاللاَّمِ، وَحُرُوفِ الْخَفْضِ، وَهِيَ: مِنْ، وَإِلَى، وَعَنْ، وَعَلَى، وَفِي، وَرُبَّ، وَالْبَاءُ، وَالْكَافُ، وَاللاَّمُ، وَحُرُوفُ الْقَسَمِ، وَهِيَ: الْوَاوُ، وَالْبَاءُ، وَالتَّاءُ.
lessons.translation: The noun is known by [accepting] khafḍ (the genitive case), tanwīn, the entry of the definite article al-, and the genitive-causing particles, which are: min, ilā, ʿan, ʿalā, fī, rubba, the bāʾ, the kāf, the lām, and the particles of oath, which are: the wāw, the bāʾ, and the tāʾ.
lessons.explanation: Rather than defining the noun by its meaning alone, Ibn Ājurrūm gives four practical tests any student can apply to a word to check whether it is an ism. If a word can take khafḍ (a kasrah-type genitive ending, e.g. after a preposition), can take tanwīn (the two-sound ending -un/-an/-in), can have الـ prefixed to it, or can follow one of the genitive-causing particles listed, then it is a noun. Verbs and particles cannot take any of these. This is one of the most-quoted lines of the whole matn, because it turns 'what is a noun?' from an abstract question into a simple, repeatable test.

keyTerms.definition: The grammatical case of a noun typically following a preposition or in an iḍāfah construction; also called جرّ.
The extra -n sound (ـٌ ـً ـٍ) attached to the end of many indefinite nouns.
The prefix الـ that makes a noun definite; it can only attach to nouns.

examples.irabAnswer: الْبَيْتِ: اسمٌ مجرورٌ بـ«في» وعلامة جرّه الكسرةُ الظاهرة على آخره.

examples.translation: A book (note the tanwīn -un, and the ability to add al- to make الكتاب).

recallQuestions.questionEnglish: Name the four signs by which a noun is recognised.
recallQuestions.correctAnswer: الخفض (accepting the genitive case), التنوين (nunation), دخول الألف واللام (taking the definite article), and following one of the حروف الخفض (genitive-causing particles).

recallQuestions.questionEnglish: Which of these particles is a genitive-causing particle (حرف خفض)?
Why can 'من' (min) never itself be a noun, no matter how it is used?
recallQuestions.correctAnswer: Because it is one of the fixed particles of khafḍ - it never takes tanwīn, khafḍ, or al-, and it never has meaning except attached to a following noun.

memorisationSections.arabicText: فَالاِسْمُ يُعْرَفُ بِالْخَفْضِ، وَالتَّنْوِينِ، وَدُخُولِ الأَلِفِ وَاللاَّمِ، وَحُرُوفِ الْخَفْضِ.
memorisationSections.translation: The noun is known by khafḍ, tanwīn, the entry of al-, and the particles of khafḍ.

lessons.matnArabic: وَالْفِعْلُ يُعْرَفُ بِقَدْ، وَالسِّينِ، وَسَوْفَ، وَتَاءِ التَّأْنِيثِ السَّاكِنَةِ.
lessons.translation: And the verb is known by [the possibility of prefixing] qad, sīn, sawfa, and the silent tāʾ of the feminine.
lessons.explanation: Just as the noun had four tests, the verb has four tests of its own - though in practice they apply mainly to identifying the past and present tense. قَدْ can precede a past or present verb (قد قامَ، قد يقومُ). السين and سوف only precede present-tense verbs and give them a future sense (سيقوم، سوف يقوم). The 'silent tāʾ of the feminine' (تاء التأنيث الساكنة) attaches to the end of a past-tense verb to show the doer is feminine (قامَتْ - 'she stood'). No noun or particle can ever accept any of these four markers, which is what makes them reliable tests.

keyTerms.definition: A particle placed before a verb; with the past tense it means 'certainly/already', with the present it means 'sometimes/perhaps'.
Particles prefixed only to present-tense verbs to give them future meaning.
A silent tāʾ suffixed to a past-tense verb to indicate its subject is feminine.

examples.translation: Hind stood (feminine subject, marked by the silent tāʾ on the verb).
examples.irabAnswer: قَامَتْ: فعلٌ ماضٍ، والتاء للتأنيث. هِنْدٌ: فاعلٌ مرفوعٌ وعلامة رفعه الضمة.

recallQuestions.questionEnglish: List the four signs by which a verb is recognised.
recallQuestions.correctAnswer: قد، والسين، وسوف، وتاء التأنيث الساكنة (qad, sīn, sawfa, and the silent feminine tāʾ).

recallQuestions.questionEnglish: 'سَوْفَ' can only ever attach to which tense of verb?

memorisationSections.arabicText: وَالْفِعْلُ يُعْرَفُ بِقَدْ، وَالسِّينِ، وَسَوْفَ، وَتَاءِ التَّأْنِيثِ السَّاكِنَةِ.
memorisationSections.translation: The verb is known by qad, sīn, sawfa, and the silent feminine tāʾ.

lessons.matnArabic: وَالْحَرْفُ مَا لاَ يَصْلُحُ مَعَهُ دَلِيلُ الاِسْمِ وَلاَ دَلِيلُ الْفِعْلِ.
lessons.translation: And the particle is that with which neither the proof of the noun nor the proof of the verb is valid.
lessons.explanation: Having given positive tests for the noun and the verb, Ibn Ājurrūm defines the particle negatively: it is whatever fails both sets of tests. A particle can never take tanwīn, khafḍ, or al- (the noun tests), and it can never take qad, sīn, sawfa, or the feminine tāʾ (the verb tests). This elegant definition-by-elimination completes the three-way division of kalām introduced in the first lesson.

keyTerms.definition: A word identified by failing every test of the noun and every test of the verb.

examples.translation: Examples of particles: hal (interrogative), lam (negates the past), inna (emphasis), wa (and).

recallQuestions.questionEnglish: How does the matn define الحرف? Why is it defined differently from the noun and the verb?
recallQuestions.correctAnswer: It is defined negatively, as whatever cannot take any sign of the noun and cannot take any sign of the verb - because particles have no single positive marker of their own.

recallQuestions.questionEnglish: Which word below is a حرف (particle)?

memorisationSections.arabicText: وَالْحَرْفُ مَا لاَ يَصْلُحُ مَعَهُ دَلِيلُ الاِسْمِ وَلاَ دَلِيلُ الْفِعْلِ.
memorisationSections.translation: The particle is that with which neither the proof of the noun nor the proof of the verb is valid.

irabExercises.translation: Knowledge is light, and ignorance is darkness.
